title: 16.5 million NASDAQ filter tests.
snippet:
16.5 million NASDAQ filter tests.

One condition won.

Lowest(CCI(27), 18) < –100

Plain English:
only take the long breakout if CCI(27) already dipped below –100
somewhere in the last 18 bars.

Across 1,000 strategy variations:

> Net profit improved on 69%
> Average trade +22% on more than half
> Bounce index: 57.8%
  (that many losing variations turned profitable)

On the base NASDAQ breakout:

7.53 → 8.6 profit/drawdown
$116 → $149 average trade

A breakout after a real washout has room.
A breakout into already-extended strength fades.

Have you ever filtered breakouts with CCI, or do you only use it as a regular oscillator?

title: The cool part about having an auto updating portfolio tracker is I can check it whenever and learn whatever I want about
snippet:
The cool part about having an auto updating portfolio tracker is I can check it whenever and learn whatever I want about my portfolio. 

And with AI it’s super easy to add new plots and calculations if I want to see something different. 

for example I wanted to understand more about the current drawdown I’m in and what the probabilities are for the near and longer term future of outcomes. 

Things like:
What’s the expected drawdown distribution over X timeframe.

How long will it take to recover from X drawdown. 

What’s the probability of new all time highs within X days based on the current drawdown. 

I know you can’t predict the future in markets, but understanding probabilities and potential outcomes that update every day automatically is pretty handy for making decisions.

title: A couple months ago I decided to start tracking my portfolio performance publicly.
snippet:
A couple months ago I decided to start tracking my portfolio performance publicly. 

https://t.co/ADiVYt6iBk

I decided to do it for the following reasons:

I can't hide a drawdown or lie about my performance when it’s automatically updated daily in a public forum. It keeps me honest. 

It also prevents me from making excuses. I can’t push stuff off when my performance is public. I need to keep progressing and working hard to ensure my performance continues to improve . 

It also helps me understand when my portfolio performs well and when it struggles. It helps me figure out where to expand next.

I used to do all my portfolio performance tracking by hand. Now I have it auto updating every day with more data than I could ever calculate by hand. I can directly use that data to make informed portfolio decisions.

title: RT @TradeQuantiX: Something that I think is funny is the rapid increase in AI based backtesters popping up everywhere.
snippet:
RT @TradeQuantiX: Something that I think is funny is the rapid increase in AI based backtesters popping up everywhere. 

I see posts on these all the time and I get emails asking me to shill them a few times a month. 

It’s funny because backtesting has been readily available for 10+ years if not more. And yet most traders are not profitable. 

Yet with AI, the ability to build basically anything becomes possible to anyone. 

So what do developers do? They don’t solve the real problems traders have. 

No. 

They make…. more backtesters. 

Except this one is “ai powered” because for whatever reason that makes it better and will finally make traders profitable. 

Access to backtesters is not the cause of unprofitability. I’d argue the backtest is the easiest part. 

It’s that nobody knows how to do any of the work pre-backtest to even find something to exploit and how to make simple crude models to show if it’s likely real or noise. 

I don’t see anyone making tools to solve this problem.
